name: Bouteloua

project_scope.note: B002 established the original four-species comparison set; B078 added B. hirsuta, B. pectinata, and B. trifida. The older source name Bouteloua hirsuta var. pectinata is represented by canonical B. pectinata rather than duplicated.

shared_traits: inflorescences built from short unilateral spicate branches/racemes
spikelets arranged mainly along one side of each branch
narrow linear leaf blades typical of Chloridoideae grasses
priority: branch length, width, curvature, and whether branches are appressed
whether branches are spaced down a long axis or clustered near the top
naked branch-tip projections beyond the spikelets
male versus female inflorescence differences in buffalograss
study_strategy.warning: Do not identify Bouteloua from leaf color or overall 'grassiness.' Start with growth form and inflorescence architecture, then use branch-tip, awn, and hair characters.

quick_key.if: creeping stoloniferous sod; male and female inflorescences strongly different, with female clusters low and bur-like
many short oat-like racemes spaced down one side of a long central axis
tufted perennial; usually 1–4 comb-like branches and conspicuous papillose-based hairs near leaf bases; branch tip continues naked beyond terminal spikelets
taller, more robust hairy-grama relative with usually 3–5 longer straight to slightly curved combs, roughly 2.5–4.5 cm; old source names include B. hirsuta var./subsp. pectinata
about 5–9 very short fuzzy/awned branches clustered near the top
small wiry reddish plant with 2–7 narrow red/purplish branches held close to the main axis and three short awns on spikelets

fast_fill_note: FAST-FILL status: B. curtipendula 4; B. dactyloides 3; B. gracilis 3; B. hirsuta 3; B. trifida 2; B. rigidiseta 1; B. pectinata 0. Remaining gaps are source-limited presentation gaps, not scientific uncertainty. Do not substitute older varietal imagery for current B. pectinata without exact-concept verification.
taxonomy_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Bouteloua pectinata Feath. as a species native from Oklahoma to Texas and Mexico. Older treatments use Bouteloua hirsuta var. pectinata or B. hirsuta subsp. pectinata; the project preserves those source names as aliases but uses one canonical B. pectinata learner.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: trace the WHOLE seed-head axis. Count one-sided comb branches, note whether they are spread down a long stem or clustered at the tip, then magnify branch tips and awns. Before calling it buffalograss, check for creeping stolons and separate male versus female heads. Leaf color is not a reliable key.
shared_morphology: Warm-season C4 grasses with narrow blades, a blade–sheath collar and small spikelets grouped on one-sided spicate branches.
A 'comb' is a short inflorescence branch; the tiny units attached to it are spikelets, each enclosed by glumes. Count whole branches before counting spikelets.
Growth form varies: B. dactyloides spreads by stolons; the other study species are chiefly tufted. Male and female buffalograss inflorescences differ strongly.

species_comparison_matrix.character: One-sided inflorescence branch count and distribution
species_comparison_matrix.curtipendula: Many short branches spaced down a long central axis
species_comparison_matrix.dactyloides: Sex-specific heads; female low bur-like clusters, not a typical tall comb array
species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Usually 1–3 longer curved combs near top
species_comparison_matrix.rigidiseta: About 5–9 short fuzzy/awned branches clustered at top
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Ranges overlap; count several mature inflorescences and inspect their attachment points.

species_comparison_matrix.hirsuta: Comb-like, often naked projection past terminal spikelets
species_comparison_matrix.pectinata: Straighter to slightly curved, roughly 2.5–4.5 cm long
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Branch shape varies with age and wind; hirsuta vs pectinata requires hairs and spikelets too.

species_comparison_matrix.hirsuta: Conspicuous papillose-based hairs near leaf base; check naked branch tip
species_comparison_matrix.pectinata: Hairy-grama relative; measure longer branches and inspect hair arrangement
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Hair/awn details are not proven by distant habit photos; photograph with mm scale.

species_comparison_matrix.dactyloides: Creeping stoloniferous sod; separate male and female inflorescences
species_comparison_matrix.other_study_species: Primarily tufted graminoids; ordinary comb-like reproductive branches
species_comparison_matrix.caution: Young mown plants may obscure growth form; do not mistake female buffalograss burs for seedheads of another genus.

anatomy_lessons.title: 1 · Read the full flowering axis
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Count the one-sided comb branches from bottom to top. Sideoats grama spreads many little oat-like branches along a long axis; blue grama often has 1–3 curved eyebrows; Texas grama has roughly 5–9 short fuzzy units near the top.
anatomy_lessons.measurement: Count complete mature branches on several stems; B. pectinata typically has 3–5 branches around 2.5–4.5 cm long.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Matched full mature inflorescences of curtipendula, gracilis, rigidiseta and pectinata with cm scale.
anatomy_lessons.caution: Cropping the bottom of the axis can make sideoats grama look like a few-branched grama.

anatomy_lessons.title: 2 · Comb-tip and papillose hair macro
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: At the tip of a mature comb, check whether the axis extends naked beyond the last spikelet. Also inspect the leaf base and spikelet hairs: these are the useful fine structures in the hairy-grama group.
anatomy_lessons.measurement: Show naked tip and individual hair bases beside a millimeter scale; count branches and measure their lengths separately.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Matched hirsuta versus pectinata branch-tip and basal-hair macros; do not substitute old hirsuta var. pectinata media without exact-concept review.
anatomy_lessons.caution: Hairiness and comb count can overlap; a generic tuft image does not prove either feature.

anatomy_lessons.title: 3 · Awning and spikelet structure
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Dissect a mature one-sided branch. Find a single spikelet and distinguish its enclosing glumes from the slender awns. B. trifida has three short awns, while B. rigidiseta appears very fuzzy/awned at the branch scale.
anatomy_lessons.measurement: Count awns on multiple mature intact spikelets at 10–20× with a 1-mm scale.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Matched rigidiseta and trifida spikelet dissections with labeled glume/awn positions after pixel verification.
anatomy_lessons.caution: Anthers, detached bristles and immature spikelets can mimic awns in distant photos.

anatomy_lessons.title: 4 · Buffalograss: stolons and two sexes
anatomy_lessons.plain_language: Trace horizontal aboveground runners to see buffalograss sod. Then compare anthers in a male head with the low, bur-like female flowering/fruiting clusters; these may be on separate plants.
anatomy_lessons.measurement: Include 1-cm ruler beside stolon nodes and matched male/female heads; photograph attachment to the same identified plant.
anatomy_lessons.photo_role: Dactyloides stolon node plus male and female reproductive close-ups, compared against an ordinary Bouteloua comb.
anatomy_lessons.caution: A male-only or female-only photograph cannot teach the full buffalograss reproductive pattern.
